newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end off lows as Wall Street steadies.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end off lows as Wall Street steadies.

text.p: French stocks closed lower on Friday, but above their session lows, after Wall Street appeared to be recovering from the previous day's slide which triggered selloffs in equities markets around the world.
Traders said the bourse looked oversold after a correction of nearly eight percent in the past 10 days, though it remains very vulnerable to volatility on Wall Street.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished down 8.70 points, or 0.39 percent, at 2,203.41 after a partial recovery from its early fall to as low as 2,171.57.
Volume was a heavy 5.9 billion francs.

The bourse was also helped by a rise in bond prices and in the franc after European Union leaders struck a deal on Friday on a pact to enforce budget discipline after its planned monetary union is launched in 1999.
For the week, the CAC index finished down 1.66 percent.
The CAC-40 December futures contract finished down 5.5 points at 2,209.5. It was up 28 points at 2,215 in the first 30 minutes of after-hours trading on GLOBEX.
* Lagardere shares posted the biggest loss on the CAC, falling 2.33 percent to 147 francs as investors wondered whether it would succeed in acquiring Thomson-CSF.

Analysts said they still believe Lagardere is the favoured candidate to acquire Thomson-CSF after the government's decision this week to relaunch the privatisation of Thomson SA and sell the Thomson-CSF unit first and money-losing Thomson Multimedia later. But they said the government's decision to sell the two branches separately could attract more offers for Thomson-CSF.
"The process will be more open, and we can't rule out other bidders," a trader said. Thomson-CSF closed down 0.64 percent.
* Shares in retailer Casino rose 0.5 percent to 246.50 francs on persistent speculation that it may be taken over or sell its hypermarkets activities, brokers said.

* Shares in Zodiac, which makes airplane evacuation slides and inflatable dinghies, also bucked the weaker trend after the company predicted double-digit earnings growth for 1996/97. They rose 0.81 percent to 1,500 francs.

* Shares in French building companies fell after an industry association and a government study showed as many as 30,000 workers could lose their jobs in the industry because of slow business. Bouygues shares fell 2.2 percent to 534 francs. It said on Thursday it proposed to buy Saint-Gobain's Cise unit for 2.16 billion francs if a planned merger of the companies' Cise and Saur units went through.
Traders say the market's near-term outlook hangs largely on Wall Street's performance.

Optimists say current prices on the bourse present buying opportunities while others see more scope for consolidation before the market resumes its advance on expectations of higher economic growth in 1997.
Key events next week include the U.S. Federal Reserve Open Market Committee Meeting and annual news conferences of the Bank of France and Bundesbank.
